column1: # One rule per row. `find` is replaced by `replace` in ONE file, on ONE side,
# and `measure/perturb_check.py` then runs the whole catalogue. A row marked
# `red` must produce at least one disagreement; a row marked `not_discriminated`
# must produce none, and the catalogue document says why no query can tell that
# rule apart. find/replace are JSON strings.
# Rows whose file is `catalogue_parse.py` are the SHARED module. A wrong rule
# there moves both answers together, so no comparison can see it; what makes
# those rows go red is `measure/parse_vectors.tsv`, the tree each rule must
# produce written out by hand. That is why what a duration unit is worth in
# nanoseconds is no longer in that module: review round 5 changed the shared
# `ms` multiplier from 10^6 to 10^3 and every answer still agreed.
